On Mon, Apr 21, 2028 at 09:18 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Team — urgent. HelmBridge reporting production impact; they want an exec update in ~4 hours.

We ran an initial telemetry sweep during the 09:30 war-room. Findings (short):
- p95 up from 220ms -> 680ms; p99 up from 480ms -> 1.9s on route /v1/generate
- GPU utilization at 86% across pool A, memory pressure on node g4-12 is high and there are intermittent kernel OOMs reported by the device driver
- Request QPS spiked 2.6x due to a customer-side batch retry loop after initial 504s

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Enabled conservative autoscale + added two warm instances (scaling group alpha) — QPS relief observed within 2 minutes
2) Enabled KV prefix caching for frequent user flows to reduce decode token work
3) Applied a temporary routing policy to divert ~25% of traffic to a compatible v2 model with slightly different quantization (lower latency, matched eval)

Dropping telemetry snapshot to shared Drive: telemetry_snapshot.json (small)

Working next: root-cause on kernel OOMs (possible model memory spike), and confirm whether retries are client-side loops we can help suppress.

-M
Marissa Cole
Sr. Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry_snapshot.json

Subject: Redwood update — HelmBridge throughput & latency stabilization plan

Elena / Tom,

Thank you for flagging the issue this morning. Brief summary and commitments: 

What happened:
- At ~08:55 PT we observed a sudden QPS increase combined with client-side retries which pushed GPU memory over transient thresholds on a subset of nodes, triggering kernel-level OOMs and increased latency/504s.

What we did immediately:
- Scaled warm capacity and added two instances to absorb load
- Enabled KV prefix caching for the most common request patterns
- Temporarily routed 25% of traffic to a compatible, lower-latency model variant to preserve availability

Customer-facing commitments (next 72h):
- Full root-cause report by 2028-04-24 17:00 PT
- Weekly cadence with your platform team during remediation until closed
- Investigation into pattern causing client-side retries and recommendation to avoid mass simultaneous retries
- Proactive configuration change to autoscale thresholds for your fleet to reduce cold pressure

Immediate ask from HelmBridge: confirm whether you want Redwood to pursue an automatic retry-suppression header (we can offer a short patch you insert server-side).

We will schedule an exec sync tomorrow for a short readout.

Regards,
David Kim
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
